The SpaceX IPO: Science Fiction or Serious Investment? | The Weekly Wrap

Recorded May 28 and published May 29, this wrap challenges SpaceX proposed valuation using segment economics, index mechanics and a comparison with established technology businesses. It also discusses Salesforce accounting, Dell demand and the contrasting economics of banks and ratings agencies.

YouTube · 2026-05-29 ↗Substack · 2026-05-29 ↗
The segment-level skepticism and insistence on treating stock compensation as a real cost are useful. The claim that Nasdaq conspired to guarantee success is not established, and the float cap is described without its full-cap weighting context. Bank of America margin improvement regardless of Fed policy is also too categorical.

substack-202957175-c019 · forecast

Bank of America low-yield securities rolling off should improve net interest margin over several years regardless of Fed policy.

Mixed
Source · 16:08-16:26 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceasserted
HorizonSeveral years after May 2026
Materialitymajor

Reinvestment can help, but deposit repricing, loan yields, mix and the rate path can offset that benefit. Regardless of policy is stronger than the balance-sheet mechanism supports.

Conditional reasoning

Higher asset yield can be offset by a greater increase in funding cost or a change in asset mix. One side of the balance sheet cannot guarantee margin direction under every rate path.

  • Net interest margin equals net interest income divided by earning assets.

Assessment test: Model asset and liability repricing jointly under alternative curves.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: high. Assessment confidence: medium. Thesis family: bank_margin.

No independent empirical outcome evidence is attached. A principle, disclosure or unfinished forecast is not a verified investment win.

  • Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13 · 2011-01-27
    Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

How he reasons here

  • Read the S-1 rather than rely on a mission statement.
  • Separate current profitable segments from speculative addressable markets.
  • Use comparable growth and margins alongside valuation.
  • Treat stock compensation and funding needs as economic costs.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.
